name: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex with Extracutaneous Involvement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex with Extracutaneous Involvement

criteria.description: Recurrent skin blistering and erosions primarily on hands and feet triggered by minor trauma
Presence of extracutaneous involvement such as nail dystrophy, mucosal fragility, or muscular weakness
Skin biopsy showing intraepidermal cleavage within basal keratinocytes
Identification of pathogenic variants in KRT5 or KRT14 genes
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent blistering with histopathological confirmation and at least one extracutaneous manifestation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to confirm diagnosis and subtype

searchTerms: skin blisters inside epidermis caused by trauma

pathognomonic.symptomName: Nail dystrophy with thickening and fragility
searchTerms: nails that are thick and break easily

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mucosal fragility with blistering and erosions
searchTerms: mouth sores that blister and peel

occasional.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic mucosal bleeding
searchTerms: low red blood cells from bleeding
scratches and scarring on the cornea

laboratory: Anemia on complete blood count due to chronic mucosal bleeding
Elevated creatine kinase in cases with muscle involvement
imaging: Esophagram showing strictures or narrowing in gastrointestinal involvement
Echocardiogram revealing cardiomyopathy in rare cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in KRT5 or KRT14 genes confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Skin biopsy with immunofluorescence mapping showing intraepidermal cleavage
Electron microscopy demonstrating basal keratinocyte cytolysis

distinguishingFeatures: Blistering limited to skin without mucosal or muscular symptoms
Blistering occurs at the lamina lucida level
More severe mucosal involvement and scarring
Blistering below the basement membrane zone

redFlags: Severe mucosal involvement causing dysphagia or airway compromise
Rapid progression of muscle weakness or cardiomyopathy
Signs of systemic infection secondary to skin barrier disruption
references: Fine JD, et al. Inherited epidermolysis bullosa: updated recommendations on diagnosis and classification. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2020.
Orphanet Report Series: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex with extracutaneous involvement. Orphanet. 2023.
Uitto J, et al. Molecular genetics of epidermolysis bullosa simplex. Exp Dermatol. 2017.
